# Conservative image flows to a continuous Stokes permeability certificate

Producer derivation; not yet independently reviewed. The target is a reusable lower-certificate operation for image-defined porous materials, not an acquired physical permeability or a new Stokes variational principle. Closest primary operations were recovered BEFORE implementation: divergence-conforming B-splines (Evans–Hughes, 2012/2013), FFT variational permeability upper bounds (Bignonnet–Dormieux 2014; Bignonnet 2020), and conforming variational bounds generally. The operation below uses this established mathematics and makes its data/rounding/support interface explicit. Historical priority is UNKNOWN.

## 1. Continuous target and supplied geometry

The periodic cell Q has M^3 cubes of side h, M>=6, volume M^3h^3. A supplied Boolean mask F defines the open pore Omega as the interior of the union of its closed pore cubes, on the three-torus Q. There is a nonempty open solid region. Define

    V={v in H^1_periodic(Q;R^3): div v=0, v=0 a.e. in the solid}.

This whole-cell definition avoids free assumptions about boundary corner regularity. Positive solid measure supplies a Poincare inequality. For viscosity one the periodic Stokes permeability K is defined by

    f^T K f = sup_(v in V) {2 f dot <v> - <|grad v|^2>}.   (1)

Here <.> is divided by TOTAL cell volume. This convention gives <u>=Kf. With viscosity mu, <u>=Kf/mu. For divergence-free periodic fields vanishing in the solid, the integrated energies 2|sym grad v|^2 and |grad v|^2 agree. We do not substitute a Darcy coefficient for the pore-scale continuum problem.

For a measured material, an independent warranted pore inclusion Omega_model subset Omega_physical is required before transferring a lower bound to physical no-slip Stokes flow. An ordinary segmented image by itself does not prove such an inclusion. A periodized cropped image is a declared mathematical cell, not a proven representative volume of the rock.

## 2. Exact discrete currents, INCLUDING winding flows

Let A be the one-cell Chebyshev erosion of F, with periodic neighbors: a cube is active only if all its 27 neighboring cubes, including itself, belong to F. Make one directed edge for every adjacent active pair in each positive coordinate direction. A current q_e is a mean normal VELOCITY coefficient, not a flux integral. # Exact complementary-energy upper on the original pore cell

Producer continuation. Same original centered48-cube periodic image, same voxel size and Stokes convention as ../PROOF.md. No new pore image, crop, continuum discretization grid or physical assumption is introduced. Equilibrated H(div) stresses, complementary-energy bounds and pressure-robust Stokes error estimation are established ordinary methods; see Lederer–Merdon, arXiv:2008.05816v2, sections1-2. The aim is a finite executable upper using these methods, not a new variational principle.

## 1. Upper principle with pressure and boundary conventions

Use the lower package's whole-cell space V of periodic H1 divergence-free velocities zero in the ORIGINAL solid. Let sigma be a tensor with each row in periodic H(div,Q), satisfying div sigma=f in all original fluid cubes. Its divergence in solid cubes is unrestricted. This supplies the solid counterforce needed for the integral of a periodic divergence to vanish; setting div sigma=f everywhere on the torus would be impossible for nonzero f.

For every v in V, integration by parts gives

    f dot <v> = -<sigma:grad v>_fluid
              = -<dev(sigma):grad v>_fluid.

Here dev sigma=sigma-(tr sigma)I/3. There is no boundary traction assumption at a fluid/solid face: v has zero trace there. A globally H(div) extension makes all interior face terms cancel, and the outer terms cancel by periodicity. Normal tractions at pore walls need not vanish. Solid stress has zero pairing with v and is not included in the energy.

The energy convention is int|grad v|^2. Although it equals int2|sym grad v|^2 for admissible velocities, sigma is a NONSYMMETRIC pseudostress. Its antisymmetric part may NOT be discarded, and there is NO factor1/2 in the bound below. Cauchy plus 2ab-b^2<=a^2 yields

    f^T K f <= <|dev sigma|^2>_fluid.              (U1)

The pressure freedom is retained by the deviatoric projection. For three equilibrated fields sigma^(k) with div sigma^(k)=e_k, linear combination supplies every f and gives the full tensor upper

    K <= U,  U_kl=<dev sigma^(k):dev sigma^(l)>_fluid.  (U2)

A scalar-Poisson construction is a valid initial upper, but is not assumed tight. The continued optimization minimizes the deviatoric norm across all row-wise RT0 stress variables.

# Same-image continuum transport bracket

The original periodic 48^3 pore cell now has a finite exact tensor enclosure

    L <= K_original <= U <= (231/20) L,

where L is the frozen, root-reviewed solenoidal-spline lower tensor. These are Loewner inequalities for every force vector, with the gradient-form unit-viscosity convention and total-cell volume normalization. Root whole-read and accepted the upper proof, numerical generator, separate exact consumer and actual receipts at this model-side scope; see ROOT_REVIEW.txt. The large solve and exact consumer were not rerun for review.

In voxel-squared units the upper tensor is approximately

    [[0.1586469283364664, 0.0101268402014091, 0.0130005654853557],
     [0.0101268402014091, 0.1226683579942858, 0.0138108808826480],
     [0.0130005654853557, 0.0138108808826480, 0.1240937185715633]].

All entries are stored as exact rational numbers in UPPER_CERTIFICATE.json. The sharp generalized factor for these two retained tensors lies in [11.542365186920506,11.542365186945062]; the simple certified factor is 11.55. The broad interval does not establish high-accuracy continuum permeability. The existing lower floor K >= .01 h^2 I remains valid, with the supplied h=5.345 micrometres.

## Acquired operation

Nine row-wise RT0 stress fields are defined on every original voxel face adjacent to fluid. No pore erosion or stress smoothing is used by this upper. Each fluid-cell divergence is repaired to the exact prescribed force using an integer tree-to-wall correction; the solid supplies the necessary counterforce on the periodic torus. A separate consumer checks all original faces, all nine integer force components, the wall totals and the original public image, then integrates the full deviatoric RT0 energy exactly. It imports neither numerical producer. This makes the result a continuum upper rather than a finite-element point prediction.

The ordinary scalar-Poisson initializer gives the exact isotropic upper 1.8556044293307536 I in voxel-squared units. Taking its deviatoric part gives a tensor with all-force bracket factor 151.24. The optimized, exactly repaired tensor Loewner improves that starting tensor and reduces the factor to 11.55. This is a comparison with the implemented initializer, not evidence of superiority over established equilibrated Stokes/FEM/FFT methods.
